issue: Stem does not fix the time convention or the fiscal year-end. 'DDB with a partial-year convention' names no convention, so distractor (d) $16,000 is correct under a half-year convention (a common partial-year convention) and (a) $32,000 is correct under a full-year-in-year-of-acquisition convention. Nothing says the company is on a calendar year, so 'Year 1' may not be 3 months.
evidence: Months held, calendar year: 80,000 x 40% x 3/12 = 8,000 (key c). Half-year convention: 80,000 x 40% x 1/2 = 16,000 (= d). Full year in the year of acquisition: 80,000 x 40% = 32,000 (= a). Compare far-dep-24 and far-dep-01, which do say 'calendar-year company' / 'calendar year'.
source: ASC 360-10-35-4 (systematic and rational allocation); the time convention (months held, half-year, full-year) is an entity policy and must be stated for a single answer.
fix: Reword: 'A calendar-year company buys an $80,000 asset (5-year life, no salvage) on October 1, Year 1, and depreciates it by DDB, computing depreciation for the months held. What is Year 1 depreciation?' Re-explain (d) as 'That uses a half-year convention (80,000 x 40% x 1/2)' with trap wrong-rule.

issue: This pure-recall item is labeled skill 'analysis', difficulty 3. It asks only for the rule that a composite-method retirement gives no gain or loss. Its near-twin far-dep-14 (same facts) is labeled application, difficulty 2. The label is two levels too high and pushes up the module's analysis share.
evidence: The stem needs no computation (calc false) and no comparison of interrelated data. The answer is the bare rule: no gain or loss, with the difference to accumulated depreciation. Under the Blueprint, recalling a rule is Remembering & Understanding, not Analysis.
source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints 2026, skill definitions (R&U vs Analysis); FAR skill allocation R&U 5-15%, Analysis 35-45%.
fix: Relabel skill remembering, difficulty 1. Better, replace the item, since it duplicates far-dep-14 (see the duplicate finding): e.g., a composite-rate computation (total annual straight-line depreciation / total cost, applied to the group).

issue: The skill and difficulty labels are inflated across the second half of the practice set. Single-step depreciation computations are labeled analysis, difficulty 3, while identical or harder items elsewhere in the module are labeled application, difficulty 1-2. far-dep-20, a recall item, is labeled application.
evidence: dep-21 has the same facts and key as exam item far-x2-28, which is labeled application/2. dep-23 is one-step units of production (90,000/300,000 x 45,000), yet labeled analysis/3, while dep-11 (one-step straight-line) is application/1. dep-24 (12,000 x 9/12) is analysis/3. dep-25 gives the depreciation to the sale date, leaving 28,000 - (80,000 - 55,000). dep-27 is the same pattern as dep-04, which is application/2. dep-28 (DDB salvage floor) is at most application/3. dep-20 (a fully depreciated asset stays at cost less accumulated depreciation) is pure recall. The module's practice+exam pool reads analysis 10/31 (32%); after relabeling it is about 2/31 (dep-10, dep-18).
source: AICPA 2026 Blueprint skill definitions; content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation.
fix: Set dep-21, 22, 25 and 27 to application/2; dep-23 and dep-24 to application/1; dep-28 to application/3; dep-20 to remembering/1. If the module needs analysis-level practice, add genuine items, e.g., finding the error in a depreciation schedule, or reconciling the fixed-asset register to the GL.

issue: There are two verbatim duplicate pairs within the module. far-dep-chk1 (lesson check) and far-dep-16 (practice) are the same item. far-dep-14 and far-dep-26 are the same composite-retirement item. A learner who did the lesson check meets the practice item again, already knowing the answer.
evidence: chk1 and dep-16 both use $60,000 cost, $6,000 salvage, a 3-year life and SYD Year 2, with the same option set {27,000; 20,000; 9,000; 18,000} and key 18,000. dep-14 and dep-26 both have a $10,000 asset retired for $2,000 under the composite method, options {8,000 loss; no gain or loss; 2,000 gain; loss for book value}, key 'no gain or loss'.
source: Review brief s2 check 7 (duplicates).
fix: Replace dep-16 with an SYD item whose depreciation years straddle fiscal years (the lesson teaches this allocation but no item tests it), e.g., a 5-year asset bought April 1: Year 2 = 30,000 x 5/15 x 3/12 + 30,000 x 4/15 x 9/12. Replace dep-26 with a composite-rate computation.

issue: Two exam-pool (mock) items reproduce material the learner has already worked. far-x2-28 is a verbatim duplicate of practice item far-dep-21. far-x2-09 uses exactly the numbers of the lesson's faded example. Mock scores on these items measure recall of a seen answer.
evidence: x2-28 and dep-21 both use $50,000 cost, $5,000 salvage, a 5-year life and DDB Year 2, key $12,000, sharing distractors $10,800 and $9,000. x2-09: cost 80,000, AD 50,000, FV 36,000, 10,000 cash paid, gain 6,000. The lesson's faded block uses the same old van (80,000 / 50,000 / 36,000 + 10,000 cash) with answers 30,000, 6,000 and 46,000.
source: Review brief s2 check 7 (duplicates); s3 mock exams (validity).
fix: Rewrite x2-28 so the salvage floor binds (e.g., Year 3 of a 4-year DDB asset with high salvage). Rewrite x2-09 with new numbers, or turn it into an exchange lacking commercial substance with boot received, or one with boot of at least 25%.

issue: The same case is over-tested: a nonmonetary exchange with commercial substance plus cash paid, asking for the new asset cost and/or the gain or loss. It is tested the same way at least 4 times across far-depreciation and far-ppe-acquisition, plus the lesson's faded example. Related rules get thin coverage: boot of 25% or more (monetary exchange) is never tested, and a proportional gain with boot received appears once (dep-10).
evidence: Same pattern: far-dep-07 (CA 50,000, FV 40,000, +15,000 cash), far-x2-09 (CA 30,000, FV 36,000, +10,000), far-ppe-24 (BV 30,000, FV 40,000, +10,000) and far-x2-34 (CA 40,000, FV 50,000, +10,000, tagged far-ppe-acquisition), plus the lesson's faded block. The 25% boot rule is taught in the lesson flowchart and fc7 but is tested by no item.
source: Review brief s2 check 7 (same fact tested the same way more than about 3 times); ASC 845-10-25-6 (boot of 25% or more = monetary exchange).
fix: Convert far-x2-09 (or dep-07) to a boot-of-25%-or-more case (e.g., boot 30% of total consideration, so the full gain is recognized), or to an exchange lacking commercial substance where boot is paid and the new asset is recorded at carrying amount plus boot.

issue: The lesson never teaches topics that four practice items test: composite/group depreciation (dep-14, dep-26), amortizing leasehold improvements over the shorter of useful life and remaining lease term (dep-19), and the half-year convention (dep-15). No other FAR lesson teaches them either.
evidence: A grep of content/far/modules/*/lesson.md for 'composite', 'leasehold' and 'half-year' finds no teaching passage; 'leasehold' appears only in an impairment example. The lesson covers only straight-line, DDB, SYD, units of production, months-held proration, changes in estimate, depletion, disposals and exchanges.
source: Review brief s3 (lesson-item alignment); ASC 842-20-35-12 (leasehold improvements).
fix: Add a short section 'Other depreciation topics'. Composite/group methods: composite rate = total annual straight-line depreciation / total cost; on a retirement, debit cash for proceeds and accumulated depreciation for cost minus proceeds, and recognize no gain or loss. Leasehold improvements: amortize over the shorter of useful life and remaining lease term, unless ownership transfers or a purchase option is reasonably certain; common-control leases use the useful life to the group (ASU 2023-01). Time conventions: months held vs half-year. Fully depreciated assets in use stay on the books with no further depreciation.

issue: The depletion base adds 'estimated restoration costs' with no qualifier. Under ASC 410-20, restoration enters the asset's cost at the fair value (usually present value) of the asset retirement obligation, as the preceding far-ppe-acquisition lesson states. The lesson, fc5 and dep-03 imply the undiscounted estimate is added. fc5 also drops the exploration costs the lesson includes.
evidence: The far-depreciation lesson says: 'Depletion base = acquisition cost + exploration and development costs + estimated restoration costs - residual value.' fc5 says: 'Cost + development + restoration - residual value.' dep-03 adds 'estimated restoration costs of $400,000' at face. The far-ppe-acquisition lesson (line 71) says: 'records the fair value of the ARO (usually a present value) as a liability and adds the same amount to the asset's cost.' A learner who meets an exam stem giving both an undiscounted estimate and its PV would pick the wrong one.
source: ASC 410-20-25-5 and 410-20-30-1 (ARO initial measurement at fair value; asset retirement cost capitalized).
fix: Lesson: '+ asset retirement cost (the ARO's fair value, usually the present value of estimated restoration costs)'. fc5: 'Cost + exploration/development + ARO (PV of restoration) - residual'. dep-03 stem: 'recognized an asset retirement obligation (present value of restoration costs) of $400,000'. The key is unchanged.

issue: Distractor (d), 'A change from the completed-contract to the percentage-of-completion method for all contracts', and its explanation 'That is a change in principle' treat a superseded ASC 605-35 policy choice as current GAAP. Under ASC 606 an entity does not elect completed-contract or POC: recognition over time vs at a point in time follows from the ASC 606-10-25-27 criteria.
evidence: ASC 606 (effective 2018/2019) superseded the ASC 605-35 construction-contract methods. The 2026 exam tests ASC 606. The key (c) is unaffected.
source: ASC 606-10-25-23 to 25-30; ASU 2014-09 (supersedes ASC 605-35 revenue guidance).
fix: Replace (d) with a current retrospective change in principle, e.g., 'A change from LIFO to FIFO inventory'. Explanation: 'A change in accounting principle, applied retrospectively (ASC 250-10-45-5).'

issue: The explanation for distractor (d) $1,250 gives the wrong derivation. It says the amount 'forces the asset to salvage in Year 3'. In fact $1,250 is the Year 4 amount; forcing the asset to salvage in Year 3 would give $7,500.
source: DDB mechanics; the item's own explanation ('Y4 is limited to 1,250').
fix: Change (d)'s explanation to: 'That is the Year 4 amount: the remaining 6,250 carrying amount less 5,000 salvage.' Trap wrong-period stays.

issue: Explanations in far-dep-11 to far-dep-28 are thin. The item-level explanations state only the rule, with no computation, although the schema calls for the full computation on calculation items. Many distractor explanations do not say how the wrong number arises, and some are non-answers.
evidence: Item-level examples: dep-12 'SYD: depreciable base x remaining life / sum of years (15).'; dep-25 'Depreciation is recorded to the disposal date before computing the gain or loss.' Distractor examples: 'Not the computation.' (dep-23 b,d; dep-27 d; dep-28 b,c); dep-28(b) $2,667 is actually straight-line, (10,000 - 2,000)/3, but is explained as 'Not the computation.'; dep-27(b) 'Use book value.' (4,333 = 26,000/6 models no stated error); dep-26(d) 'No gain or loss.'; dep-16(a) 'Use the depreciable base.'; dep-19(c) 'Divide by the shorter period.' Contrast dep-01 to dep-10, where each distractor's arithmetic is shown.
source: src/content/schema.ts (Mcq.explanation: 'overall teaching point, full computation when calculation-based'); review brief s2 check 4.
fix: For each listed item, rewrite the item-level explanation with the full computation (as in dep-01 to dep-10), and give each distractor the arithmetic of the error it models (e.g., dep-28(b): 'Straight-line: (10,000 - 2,000)/3 = 2,667').

issue: Several distractors are implausible or model no identifiable error, so they are eliminated without knowing the rule. far-dep-18 (a) also carries a stray tag, '$250,000, the midpoint': it is the only option with descriptive text, and the 'midpoint' it names is not a quantity in the problem.
evidence: dep-05(d) 'Loss of $48,000' is the accumulated depreciation figure. dep-11(b) $5,400 = 54,000/10, but no 10-year figure appears in the stem. dep-18(a) 250,000 actually models ignoring the revision (125,000 x the original $2/ton), not a midpoint; (b) $156,250 and (c) $100,000 reproduce no natural error. dep-19(c) $10,000 = 120,000/12, with no 12-year figure. dep-23(b) $30,000 and (d) $9,000 have no derivation ('Not the computation.'). dep-25(d) 'A $28,000 gain' treats proceeds as the gain.
source: Review brief s2 check 2 (each distractor definitely wrong for the reason given) and check 6 (cues).
fix: Use error-modeled values. dep-05(d): 'Gain of $22,000' (proceeds treated as the gain). dep-11(b): $10,800 (SYD Year 1, 54,000 x 9/45). dep-18: (a) '$250,000' explained as the unrevised $2/ton rate; (b) $175,000 (retroactive catch-up: 1,000,000/600,000 x 225,000 - 200,000); (c) $208,333 (original cost / revised total 600,000 tons x 125,000). dep-19(c): '$120,000 expensed in Year 1'. dep-23: $16,500 (adds salvage: 110,000 x 45/300) in place of $30,000. dep-25(d): 'A $52,000 loss' (proceeds - cost).

issue: Trap labels do not match the misconception the distractor models.
evidence: dep-13(b) $9,000 (ignores the change in estimate) is labeled 'outdated-rule'; that label is for superseded law, so it should be wrong-rule or partial-computation. dep-21(d) $20,000 and dep-22(c) $12,000 / (d) $15,000 are other-year amounts labeled 'reversed' (should be wrong-period). dep-24(a) $12,000 (full year) is labeled wrong-rule (should be wrong-period); (b) $6,000 (half-year convention) is labeled wrong-classification (should be wrong-rule). dep-17(b) $4,000 (straight-line 20% rate) is labeled distractor-number (should be wrong-rule). dep-28(b) $2,667 (straight-line) is labeled distractor-number (should be wrong-classification/wrong-rule).
source: src/content/schema.ts TRAP_TYPES; review brief s2 check 2.
fix: Relabel as listed in the evidence.

issue: The key gives away the answer. At 82 characters it is by far the longest option (the others run 46-64), the only one with universal qualifiers ('always ... whether or not'), and it repeats the stem's phrase 'commercial substance'. The stem already fixes 'lacks commercial substance', so the key also answers a broader question than the one asked.
evidence: Option lengths: a 82, b 64, c 46, d 49. Only (a) generalizes across both cases.
source: Review brief s2 check 6 (answer cues).
fix: Parallel options of similar length: (a) 'The loss is recognized in earnings immediately' (key); (b) 'The loss is deferred by reducing the new asset's cost'; (c) 'The loss is recognized only if cash is received'; (d) 'The loss is recognized in other comprehensive income'.

issue: The key reads 'Gain of $0', which is awkward; the item explanation itself says 'no gain or loss'.
evidence: Option (c) text 'Gain of $0' against the explanation '**no gain or loss**'.
source: Wording consistency.
fix: Change (c) to 'No gain or loss'.

issue: The stem does not say the lessor is unrelated. Since ASU 2023-01 (testable since 1/1/2024), leasehold improvements in a common-control lease are amortized over their useful life to the common-control group, regardless of lease term. Under that reading the answer would be $12,000.
evidence: ASU 2023-01 is listed as testable in review/reference/far-standards.md s2a. The 'shorter of useful life or lease term' rule assumes the lease is not between entities under common control.
fix: Add 'from an unrelated lessor' to the stem, and mention the common-control exception in the explanation.

issue: Two lesson citations are imprecise, and the method-change preferability requirement is never mentioned. ASC 932 is Extractive Activities - Oil and Gas; mining depletion is ASC 930. Method changes are covered in ASC 250-10-45-18 to 45-20, not 45-17; 45-19 requires that the new method be preferable.
evidence: Frontmatter citations: 'FASB ASC 250-10-45-17 (changes in estimate; method changes)'; 'FASB ASC 932 and 360 (depletion of natural resources)'. The worked-example insight says a method change is 'handled prospectively' but does not say it needs preferability justification.
source: ASC 250-10-45-17 to 45-20; ASC 930 (Extractive Activities - Mining); ASC 932 (Oil and Gas).
fix: Cite 'ASC 250-10-45-17 to 45-20' and 'ASC 930, 932 and 360'. Add to the insight: '... and, like any principle change, the new method must be justified as preferable.'

issue: The nonmonetary-exchange section covers only the commercial-substance exception to fair-value measurement. It omits the other two exceptions (fair value not determinable; an exchange of inventory to facilitate sales to customers) and the rule that the fair value of the asset received is used if it is more clearly evident.
evidence: The flowchart starts at 'Commercial substance?'; the takeaways mention no other exception.
fix: Add one line before the flowchart: 'Use carrying amount (not fair value) if fair value is not determinable, the exchange is of inventory to facilitate sales to customers, or the exchange lacks commercial substance. Use the FV of the asset received if it is more clearly evident.'

issue: Two flashcards are not atomic. fc5 packs the depletion-base composition, the rate and the COGS/inventory split into one card. fc7 packs the loss rule, the gain deferral, the proportional gain with boot and the 25% monetary threshold into one card.
evidence: fc7 back: 'Losses: recognize. Gains: defer (...), unless boot received -> proportional gain; boot >= 25% -> monetary exchange.'
source: Review brief s2 (flashcards atomic).
fix: Split fc5 into 'Depletion base' and 'Depletion: extracted vs sold'. Split fc7 into 'No commercial substance: losses vs gains' and 'Boot received: proportional gain and the 25% rule'.

issue: Several things the lesson teaches have no practice or exam MCQ in this module: SYD partial-year allocation across fiscal years, the boot-of-25%-or-more monetary rule, the depletion of extracted-but-unsold units in a roll-forward, and objective 4 (PP&E roll-forward and register-to-GL reconciliation). Objective 4 is exercised only by TBS far-tbs-u6-ppe-rollforward and far-tbs-u6-ppe-subledger (other batch).
evidence: All 31 practice and exam MCQs were mapped to lesson sections. None tests SYD straddling fiscal years, the 25% boot rule or a register-to-GL reconciliation.
source: Lesson objectives (frontmatter); review brief s3 lesson-item alignment.
fix: Use the duplicate slots (dep-16, dep-26, x2-28, x2-09) for these: an SYD fiscal-year straddle, a 25% boot exchange, and a short register-to-GL reconciling-item MCQ at analysis level.

issue: Only one pre-question (DDB Year 1) primes a lesson with three big blocks. Nothing primes disposals or nonmonetary exchanges, the module's main analysis-level objective.
evidence: Frontmatter: preQuestions: [far-dep-pre1].
source: Review brief s3 lesson design (pre-questions prime the right concept).
fix: Add a second pre-question, e.g., 'An exchange lacks commercial substance and the old asset's FV exceeds its carrying amount; no cash changes hands. Is a gain recognized?'
